title: Filtered colimits of simplicial localizations with compatible edge collections
statement: Use small simplicial sets, coherent functor categories and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and localization at a collection of edges as defined in [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty ordinary category such that every finite diagram in $I$ has a cocone. Let $(p_i:X_i\to Y_i)_{i\in I}$ be a strict diagram of maps of small simplicial sets: each arrow $a:i\to j$ gives simplicial maps $x_a:X_i\to X_j$, $y_a:Y_i\to Y_j$ with $p_jx_a=y_ap_i$, respecting identities and composition. Let $V_i\subseteq(X_i)_1$ be collections of edges with $x_a(V_i)\subseteq V_j$ for every $a:i\to j$. Suppose each $p_i$ exhibits $Y_i$ as a localization of $X_i$ at $V_i$. Form colimits degreewise, set $X=\varinjlim_iX_i$ and $Y=\varinjlim_iY_i$, let $j_i:X_i\to X$ be the colimit maps, and put $V=\bigcup_i j_i(V_i)\subseteq X_1$. Then the induced map $p:X\to Y$ exhibits $Y$ as a localization of $X$ at $V$. No injectivity of transition maps or quasicategory hypothesis on the $X_i,Y_i$ is required.

source.place: Kerodon Corollary 6.3.2.12 (05ZQ), with localization interpreted by the coherent functor-category definition already fixed in def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map. This is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag. Read online 2026-10-17; archived source WANTED.

proof.text: The cocone hypothesis makes $I$ filtered: the empty diagram gives nonemptiness, a two-object discrete diagram gives a common target, and a parallel-pair diagram gives a postcomposition making the two arrows equal. Put $T_i=p_i(V_i)$. For each transition, $y_a(T_i)=p_jx_a(V_i)\subseteq T_j$. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-existence] to the strict diagrams of pairs $(X_i,V_i)$ and $(Y_i,T_i)$. Write $L_i=X_i[V_i^{-1}]$, $M_i=Y_i[T_i^{-1}]$, with localization maps $u_i:X_i\to L_i$ and $v_i:Y_i\to M_i$ in the sense of [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map]. Strict functoriality supplies a natural transformation $q_i:L_i\to M_i$ satisfying $v_ip_i=q_iu_i$. These squares form a strict diagram; no quasi-inverses have been chosen.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.2.12, first displayed square, and Proposition 6.3.2.11.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and any test quasicategory $\mathcal E$ in a sufficiently large universe. Write $\operatorname{Fun}_{V_i}(X_i,\mathcal E)$ for the full subcategory on $V_i$-inverting diagrams, and define $\operatorname{Fun}_{T_i}(Y_i,\mathcal E)$ likewise. For every $H:Y_i\to\mathcal E$, the localization hypothesis on $p_i$ says that $Hp_i$ inverts $V_i$. Thus $H$ inverts every edge of $T_i=p_i(V_i)$, so $\operatorname{Fun}_{T_i}(Y_i,\mathcal E)=\operatorname{Fun}(Y_i,\mathcal E)$ as full simplicial subcategories. The universal property of $v_i$ therefore makes $v_i^*:\operatorname{Fun}(M_i,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(Y_i,\mathcal E)$ a coherent functor equivalence. By [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test], $v_i$ is a categorical equivalence. The universal properties of $u_i$ and $p_i$ make their restriction maps equivalences onto the same full subcategory $\operatorname{Fun}_{V_i}(X_i,\mathcal E)$. The strict equation $u_i^*q_i^*=p_i^*v_i^*$ consequently makes $q_i^*$ an equivalence: compose quasi-inverses to $u_i^*$, $p_i^*$ and $v_i^*$; the inverse equations are the whiskered inverse equations for those three maps. The same test shows that $q_i$ is a categorical equivalence. This argument is for the actual functorial $v_i,q_i$ of Step 1, so their naturality comes from that construction, not from choices of inverses.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.2.12, assertion that both the lower horizontal and right vertical maps are categorical equivalences; expanded using the coherent functor-category universal property.

proof.text: Let $k_i:Y_i\to Y$ be the colimit maps, put $V=\bigcup_i j_i(V_i)$ and $T=\bigcup_i k_i(T_i)$. The equations $k_ip_i=pj_i$ give $T=p(V)$ by taking images of each representative. Filtered-colimit compatibility in [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-existence] identifies $\operatorname{colim}_i L_i$ with $L=X[V^{-1}]$, $\operatorname{colim}_i M_i$ with $M=Y[T^{-1}]$, and the colimits of $u_i,v_i,q_i$ with the actual maps $u:X\to L$, $v:Y\to M$, $q:L\to M$, satisfying $vp=qu$. Apply [lem-coef-joyal-filtered-equivalences] separately to the natural transformations $(v_i:Y_i\to M_i)$ and $(q_i:L_i\to M_i)$ of Step 2. It yields categorical equivalences $v$ and $q$. Its hypotheses allow arbitrary simplicial sets and arbitrary, possibly non-injective, transition maps.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.2.12, second displayed square, with both applications of Corollary 4.8.8.11.

proof.text: For any test quasicategory $\mathcal E$, restriction by $u$ induces an equivalence $u^*:\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}_V(X,\mathcal E)$ by [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-existence] and [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map]. The categorical equivalences $v,q$ induce coherent functor equivalences $v^*:\operatorname{Fun}(M,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(Y,\mathcal E)$ and $q^*:\operatorname{Fun}(M,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal E)$ by [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test]. Restriction by $p$ factors through $\operatorname{Fun}_V(X,\mathcal E)$: for $H:Y\to\mathcal E$ and $w=j_i(w_i)$ with $w_i\in V_i$, one has $Hp(w)=Hk_ip_i(w_i)$, an equivalence because $p_i$ is a localization and $Hk_i$ is a test diagram. The full-subcategory definition makes this a factorization in every simplicial degree. The square gives $p^*v^*=u^*q^*$ with this codomain. If $r$ is a coherent quasi-inverse of $v^*$, then $p^*\simeq u^*q^*r$; whiskering the unit and counit of $v^*$ gives this natural equivalence. A quasi-inverse is $v^*(q^*)^{-1}(u^*)^{-1}$, with inverse equations obtained by composing the three specified unit and counit equivalences. Thus $p^*$ is the required coherent functor equivalence onto $\operatorname{Fun}_V(X,\mathcal E)$ for every $\mathcal E$, which is exactly the asserted localization.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.2.12, final inference from the square; expanded in coherent functor categories, including the right vertical equivalence.

proof_origin.place: Corollary 6.3.2.12, proof, using Proposition 6.3.2.11 and Corollary 4.8.8.11.
